Print method for 'srocsa' objects

print.srocsa.Rd

This function prints the main results: convergence of the optimizer, SAUC estimates, and parameter estimates with standard errors (SE) for each marginal selection probability \(p\). For the time-dependent results, the results are printed at each time point.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'srocsa'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted object returned by the function srocsa.t, tsroc, or tsrocsa.lrt.

digits

The digits of the results

...

Other arguments in function print.default

Value

Print the main results of a srocsa object

Details

Optimizer

1 indicates that nlminb converged (convergence = 0).

SAUC

The SE is calculated by the delta method. The confidence interval is calculated on the logit scale, so it is not symmetric around the SAUC.

tau_se, tau_sp

Between-study standard deviations (not variances).

beta, alpha

"-" indicates not applicable (\(p = 1\), or the model without selection). The SE of alpha is not available.

Results from tsroc

Shown as \(p = 1\), because tsroc fits the model without selection.

See also

srocsa.t, hattori.tsroc, tsrocsa.lrt, summary.srocsa, plot.srocsa

Examples

## load data
data(IVD)

## print the results
fit1 <- srocsa.t(TP = TP, FN = FN, TN = TN, FP = FP, data = IVD, sa.p = c(1, 0.8, 0.6))
print(fit1)
#> ==================================================
#> Model optimization
#> 
#> Number of studies : 33 
#> Optimizer         : 1 1 1 
#> 
#> * 1 indicates converged
#> ==================================================
#> 
#> SAUC Estimates
#> -------------------------------------------
#> Marginal p    SAUC      SE   CI.low   CI.up
#> -------------------------------------------
#> p = 1        0.874   0.029    0.806   0.920
#> p = 0.8      0.871   0.030    0.800   0.919
#> p = 0.6      0.822   0.041    0.727   0.889
#> 
#> ==================================================
#> 
#> Parameter Estimates (SE)
#> -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#> Marginal p           mu_se           mu_sp          tau_se          tau_sp              rho            beta         alpha
#> -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#> p = 1        1.484 (0.177)   1.824 (0.154)   0.597 (0.175)   0.826 (0.117)   -0.424 (0.236)               -             -
#> p = 0.8      1.472 (0.177)   1.818 (0.154)   0.607 (0.179)   0.828 (0.118)   -0.404 (0.241)   5.000 (5.396)    -7.943 (-)
#> p = 0.6      1.234 (0.150)   1.681 (0.153)   0.618 (0.202)   0.850 (0.127)   -0.275 (0.270)   5.000 (4.126)   -10.451 (-)
#> 

fit2 <- srocsa.t(TP = TP, FN = FN, TN = TN, FP = FP, data = IVD, sa.p = c(1, 0.8, 0.6), c11 = 0.5)
print(fit2, digits = 4)
